newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India Reliance says has no plans to import naphtha.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance says has no plans to import naphtha.

text.p: India's industry giant Reliance Industries (RIL) said on Friday it has no plans to import two million tonnes per year of light naphtha for its petrochemical cracker complex.
"While RIL was open to look at imported naphtha as an option, it has domestic feedstock available on contracted basis," the company said in a statement.

The company was responding to an earlier Reuters report quoting a company official as saying that Reliance will import two million tonnes per year (50,000 barrels-per-day) of high paraffinic naphtha for its new petrochemical cracker complex when it starts operations in December.
A. Poddar, vice-president of projects at Reliance had told Reuters by telephone, "We will import all the requirements."
Industry sources had said that Reliance earlier planned to obtain half of the two million tonnes it requires from domestic refineries.
But Poddar had said Reliance could not source its naphtha requirements from within India as domestic refineries did not produce the right quality.
"We are looking typically for an Arabian light grade," he said.
The company was talking to a number of suppliers but no term contracts have yet been concluded, Poddar had said.
